title: Private (K8s) install notes — SIEM-ready Audit Export (beta)
content:
Context
- This doc captures install/ops notes for enabling SIEM-ready audit export in Redwood Private (Kubernetes-based) environments.
- Beta sinks supported: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3 (including some S3-compatible endpoints, see notes).
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once. Customers should dedupe by event_id (plus destination_id if needed) downstream.

High-level architecture (Private)
- Control plane service: audit-export (stores destination configs, filter rules, state, and per-destination cursor/checkpoint metadata).
- Worker subsystem: audit-export-worker (pulls from durable buffer, applies filters, delivers to sink, persists checkpoint, retries, DLQ).
- Storage:
  - Postgres: required for configuration/state + checkpoints.
  - Durable buffer: depends on Private deployment profile (see “Dependencies”); worker requires a durable queue/buffer to meet retry/delay semantics.
- Secrets: destination credentials (HEC token, Datadog API key, AWS creds, etc.) provided via K8s secret integration.

Kubernetes resources (what gets installed)
Namespaces
- Typically installed into: redwood-system (or existing control-plane namespace).
- Worker components may be separated into: redwood-audit-export (recommended if you use restrictive NetworkPolicies).

Core objects
- Deployments
  - audit-export-api (control plane API + health/status endpoints)
  - audit-export-worker (delivery workers)
- Jobs (optional, on upgrade)
  - audit-export-migrate (DB migrations; can be run as Helm hook)
- Services
  - audit-export-api ClusterIP (Console/private admin calls)
- ConfigMaps
  - exporter runtime config (batch sizes, timeouts, region endpoints, feature flags)
- Secrets
  - destination credential material (see “Secrets integration”)
- RBAC
  - ServiceAccount(s) for api/worker
  - Role/RoleBinding allowing: read specific Secrets (or ExternalSecrets), list/watch config resources, emit events
- NetworkPolicy (recommended)
  - Egress allow list for sink endpoints only (Splunk/Datadog/S3), plus DNS.

Resource sizing (starting point; tune per tenant/event volume)
- audit-export-api
  - Requests: cpu 250m, mem 512Mi
  - Limits: cpu 1, mem 1Gi
  - Replicas: 2 (for HA)
- audit-export-worker
  - Requests: cpu 500m, mem 1Gi
  - Limits: cpu 2, mem 2Gi
  - Replicas: 2–6 (depends on expected audit event rate + sink throughput)
- Notes
  - Worker is the one that will back up under throttling/5xx. Plan to scale workers horizontally, but be mindful of per-destination ordering expectations (we do not guarantee global ordering; best-effort per destination/partition).
  - If the durable buffer is shared with other services, set conservative worker concurrency to avoid cross-service contention.

Dependencies / prerequisites
Required
- Kubernetes 1.25+ (align with Private installer baseline)
- Postgres 13+ reachable from audit-export-api and workers
  - Database: redwood_audit_export (name configurable)
  - Ensure connection pool settings are compatible with N replicas.
- DNS + outbound TLS (443) for external sinks
- Clock sync (NTP) across nodes (important for time-window replay and consistent timestamps)

Durable buffer / queue
- Private deployments vary; confirm which buffering primitive is enabled:
  - Option A (preferred): Redwood “durable-queue” service enabled in Private stack (managed by installer).
  - Option B: customer-provided Kafka (topic per workspace/tenant partitioning) if already part of Private footprint.
  - Option C: Postgres-backed queue mode (supported for low-to-moderate volume only; higher latency under burst).
- Action item during install: explicitly choose the buffer backend and set the worker’s “checkpoint strategy” accordingly.

Ingress/Access
- No external ingress required for sinks (workers call out).
- audit-export-api is internal-only; Console or admin tooling talks to it via cluster networking.

Network egress requirements
General
- Worker pods need outbound connectivity to customer-managed endpoints:
  - Splunk HEC: customer Splunk base URL (typically https://splunk.example.com:8088)
  - Datadog Logs intake: https://http-intake.logs.<site> (e.g., datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, us3.datadoghq.com)
  - S3: AWS regional S3 endpoints or customer S3-compatible endpoint
- Ensure egress policies allow:
  - DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to cluster DNS
  - TCP 443 to the destination FQDNs
  - Optional: TCP 8088 for Splunk HEC if not behind 443 (common in Splunk deployments)

TLS/Proxy considerations
- If the environment uses TLS inspection proxies:
  - Confirm the worker trusts the proxy CA bundle (mount CA bundle and set SSL_CERT_FILE / Java cacerts if applicable).
  - Splunk HEC often uses private PKI; mount CA cert for the Splunk endpoint.
- If using an explicit HTTP(S) proxy:
  - Worker supports HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY (confirm in values).
  - Add internal cluster CIDRs and Postgres host to NO_PROXY.

Datadog endpoint selection
- Use site-specific endpoint. Common misconfig = using datadoghq.com for EU org.
- Rate limits: 429s are common under burst; ensure backoff/circuit breaker is enabled (see “Backpressure notes”).

S3 / S3-compatible notes
- AWS S3: allow egress to s3.<region>.amazonaws.com (or VPC endpoint if present).
- S3-compatible (MinIO/Ceph/R2, etc.):
  - Must support PUT object and list/head (depending on idempotency strategy).
  - Strongly recommended: path-style vs virtual-host-style addressing must match endpoint.
  - Confirm server-side encryption support if enabling SSE-KMS-like semantics; for non-AWS, we may fall back to SSE-S3 or client-side encryption depending on config.

Secrets integration (destination credentials)
Credential types
- Splunk HEC
  - hec_token (required)
  - hec_ack_enabled (optional) + ack polling interval
  - tls_ca_bundle (optional; required for private PKI)
- Datadog
  - api_key (required)
  - site (required)
- S3
  - Preferred (AWS): IRSA / workload identity (no static secrets in cluster)
  - Alternate: access_key_id + secret_access_key + optional session_token
  - Optional: kms_key_id (AWS) and bucket policy prerequisites

How secrets are wired in Private
- Baseline support: Kubernetes Secret references stored as “secretRef” in destination config (control plane stores reference; worker reads actual secret at runtime).
- Recommended: ExternalSecrets / Vault integration
  - Use ExternalSecrets to sync from Vault/KMS into a namespaced K8s Secret.
  - Rotate tokens/keys without redeploying (worker re-reads secret on failure/retry path; for immediate take effect, restart worker pods).

RBAC for secrets
- Worker ServiceAccount should have permission to GET only the specific secret names used by audit export in its namespace.
- Avoid broad list/watch on secrets.

Audit trail / config change logging
- Ensure Redwood audit logging is enabled in Private control plane so changes to export destinations/filters are themselves audited.
- This is important for customer compliance evidence (who changed where exports go).

Helm / installer wiring (values you’ll likely need)
(Names may change; treat as a checklist for installer config review)
- auditExport.enabled=true
- auditExport.api.replicas=2
- auditExport.worker.replicas=2
- auditExport.storage.postgres.dsn / secretRef
- auditExport.buffer.backend=durable-queue|kafka|postgres
- auditExport.network.httpProxy/httpsProxy/noProxy (if needed)
- auditExport.tls.customCaSecret (if Splunk uses private CA)
- auditExport.featureFlags.siemExportBeta=true (still gated per-tenant/workspace)

Backpressure / reliability notes (Private-specific)
- If a destination is misconfigured (401/403) workers will retry and can build backlog quickly.
  - Confirm “pause destination” is available via control plane and surfaced in Console/admin.
- Recommended defaults for Private (more conservative than Hosted):
  - Max in-flight batches per destination: low (e.g., 2–4)
  - Exponential backoff with jitter on 429/5xx
  - Circuit breaker after sustained failures (e.g., open after N failures / M minutes; auto half-open)
- Make sure exporter worker CPU/memory limits are not so tight that retries + TLS handshakes cause OOM/CPU throttling loops.

Observability prerequisites
- Metrics
  - Exporter emits: delivery_success_total, delivery_failure_total, delivery_latency_seconds (hist), backlog_depth, dlq_depth.
  - In Private: confirm metrics scraping is enabled (Prometheus or equivalent) and ServiceMonitor is installed if using Prom Operator.
- Logs
  - Worker logs include destination_id, sink_type, error_classification (auth/throttle/schema/network), and request_id where available.
  - Confirm logs are retained long enough for troubleshooting (>= 7 days recommended for beta).
- Health endpoints
  - audit-export-api: /healthz and /status (per-destination last_success_at/last_error)

Upgrade considerations
Version compatibility
- Treat audit-export components as coupled to:
  - control plane API version
  - audit event schema version (v1 in beta)
  - worker connector versions (Splunk/Datadog/S3)
- When upgrading Private stack, keep these in mind:
  - Upgrading control plane without worker can leave status reporting inconsistent.
  - Upgrading worker without API can fail if new fields are required for config parsing.

DB migrations
- Some releases may include DB migrations for destination state/checkpoint tables.
  - Run migrations as a pre-upgrade hook (Job) or as part of the installer’s migration step.
  - Ensure migration job has the same network access to Postgres as the api.

Rolling upgrades
- Recommended process
  1) (Optional) Pause high-volume destinations if you expect sink instability during upgrade window.
  2) Run DB migration job.
  3) Roll audit-export-api deployment.
  4) Roll audit-export-worker deployment.
  5) Verify status endpoints and send a test event per sink.
- At-least-once + retries means duplicates may appear around restarts; customers should dedupe.

Rollback
- Prefer rolling back worker + api in lockstep.
- DB migrations may not be reversible; verify whether a given release is “rollback-safe”. If not, rollback requires restoring DB snapshot.

Private installer upgrade gotchas
- NetworkPolicy changes frequently cause “it worked in staging but not prod” failures. If enabling policies, do it in a separate change and validate each destination.
- If using IRSA/workload identity, upgrades that change ServiceAccount name/annotations can break S3 auth.

Validation checklist (post-install)
- Control plane
  - audit-export-api pods healthy (2/2)
  - Can create destination + filter rules via Console/admin
  - Destination status fields update (last_success_at changes after test)
- Worker
  - Can deliver test event to each configured sink
  - Metrics are scraped; dashboards show non-zero counters
  - DLQ is empty in steady state
- Network
  - Egress to Splunk/Datadog/S3 works from worker namespace
  - TLS validation passes (no “unknown authority” unless expected)

Troubleshooting quick hits
- Splunk HEC 401/403 after token rotation
  - Confirm the K8s Secret updated in the namespace the worker reads from.
  - Restart worker pods if rotation needs immediate pickup.
  - If HEC ACK enabled, confirm the endpoint supports ACK and that ACK polling isn’t being blocked.
- Datadog 429s / throttling
  - Reduce batch size and concurrency.
  - Confirm correct site endpoint.
  - Verify proxy isn’t adding retries on top of our retries.
- S3 AccessDenied
  - For IRSA: confirm SA annotation and IAM role trust policy.
  - For static keys: confirm secret mounted + no whitespace issues.
  - Check bucket policy allows PutObject to the prefix used by partitioning.
- Backlog growth
  - Pause destination to stop retry storm.
  - Use replay tooling carefully (time-window-limited) and expect duplicates.

Open questions / TODOs (as of 2025-02-06)
- Confirm final buffer backend(s) supported in Private beta for higher-volume tenants (Kafka vs “durable-queue”).
- Decide default NetworkPolicy template to ship with installer (allow list FQDNs vs static IPs; FQDN policies vary by CNI).
- Document “S3-compatible” support boundaries more clearly (tested providers + encryption behavior).
- Add explicit operator doc for credential rotation without restart (do we want periodic secret re-read?).
